purpose: Reusable lemmas and operators that an agent can try on other Erdős problems. The attack graph stays the strike map; this ledger is the toolbox. A candidate match is not an implication and never sets a status.
trust: relation=discharges means the method is a kernel-checked or independently reviewed lemma used on that problem, still possibly partial. relation=candidate is a tag or OEIS shape match only. relation=obstruction is a proved failure of a naive transfer.

methods.statement: For all natural j,k: (k+1)*gcd(C(j,k), C(j+1,k+1)) = C(j,k)*gcd(k+1,j+1).

discharges.note: used in the wrap-size bound; does not close P699

methods.statement: If U|B, gcd(U,A)=1 and A*C=(j+1)*B then U|C.

discharges.note: transfers the residual wrap factor; does not close P699

remaining: size bound W < C is informal

methods.statement: For j>=3, n=2j+3, m=n/gcd(n,j) satisfies m>=3 and m divides both C(n,2) and C(n,j).

discharges.note: infinite i=2, n=2j+3 family in divisor form; prime-factor step is an Init gap
complete i=2 slice in gcd form; prime-factor step is an Init gap; does not close P699

methods.statement: If j(j-1)(j-2)<C(n,3) then gcd(C(n,3),C(n,j))>=2. If also n=3 mod 4, the gcd is odd and >=3.

discharges.note: i=3 transfer plus odd slice; size bound is elementary/Python; 2-adic residual open; does not close P699

methods.statement: For 2<=i<j and n=2j+2, some prime p>=i divides both C(n,i) and C(n,j).

discharges.note: entire d=2 line, conditional on EEES; does not close P699

methods.statement: If 2<=i<j<=n/2 and n-i < p <= n with p prime, then p divides both C(n,i) and C(n,j).

discharges.note: even-i n=2j+3 diagonal, using Nagura for i>=8

methods.statement: Periodic reduced-residue gap counts equal an inclusion-exclusion over residue covers that forbid both endpoints.

discharges.note: exact counting identity, not an asymptotic
same operator; does not determine the missing-gap spectrum

methods.statement: If H_P(z)=sum z^{g_i}, B_P(z)=sum z^{g_i+g_{i+1}} and max g_i < 2q then H_{Pq}(z)=(q-2)H_P(z)+B_P(z).

obstructions.note: at P=30030 a 22-gap exists but no 20-gap; endpoint-oblivious covers do not imply a 20-gap

methods.statement: Every finite non-path tree H occurs as the exact branch skeleton of some tree whose independence polynomial is not log-concave.

discharges.note: not non-unimodality; not a tree theorem

methods.statement: The three-hub Laurent block B(r,s,t;c,d,e) is centrally unimodal for integers r,s,t>=1 and real c,d,e>=1.

discharges.note: algebraic block only; global tree partition missing

methods.statement: Leading independence-polynomial coefficients of a pendant-P2 decoration are an exact sum over independent sets of the core, without building the huge tree.

discharges.note: exact tails, not a full polynomial
